critical_code_review_comments: server.py still 1078 lines — should be split into routers/ (auth, chapters, admin, library, sr, quiz).
fix_word_markup runs on every startup and touches all chapters; consider gating with a version flag in a metadata collection so repeat cold-starts don't re-scan the entire corpus.

Ruby.jsx splitOkurigana silently falls back to a single-ruby when the pattern doesn't match — good defensive behavior, but consider console.warn in dev to surface future DSL mismatches (e.g. new seed data with irregular okurigana).

RubyText renders the DSL string when the '|' regex matches, but a text like 'a|b' with no Japanese would still be parsed as ruby with reading 'b'. If the app ever gains non-JP content, restrict parseSpec to tokens whose head contains CJK.
No unit tests exist for splitOkurigana / parseSpec / parseParen — recommend adding a small React/JS test file so DSL parsing regressions are caught before hitting the UI.
